Write Text as UTF-8, Falling Back to ASCII on an Encoding Error

Source: R/lib_helpers.R
wrtxtfb.Rd

Writes text to path as UTF-8, one element per line. If the write fails (for example a destination or locale that cannot represent the characters), it retries with an ASCII transliteration produced by toascii(), so capsule generation never fails on a non-ASCII name. Use it to write generated text files (README, citation, script) whose content may include names with accents.

Usage

wrtxtfb(text, path)

Arguments

text

A character vector of lines to write; as.character() converts any other type.

path

The destination file, a single non-empty string. Its directory must exist.

Value

Invisibly, path.

Details

The lines are joined with "\n", a final newline is added, and the UTF-8 bytes are written through a binary connection, so the bytes on disk are UTF-8 whatever the session locale (a text connection would re-encode from the native locale) and line endings are "\n" on every platform. An existing file is overwritten. A missing element is written as the two letters NA, and an empty text writes a file holding a single newline.

The ASCII retry is taken on any error from the first write, not only on an encoding error; if the retry also fails (a directory that does not exist, a read-only location), that error reaches the caller. A path that is not a single non-empty string is refused before anything is written ("path must be a single non-empty string").

See also

toascii() for the retry's transliteration.

Examples

p <- wrtxtfb(c("line one", "line two"),
                         tempfile(fileext = ".txt"))
readLines(p)
#> [1] "line one" "line two"

# Accented names are written as UTF-8 bytes, whatever the locale.
q <- wrtxtfb("Author: \u00c1ngela Zorro Medina", tempfile())
readLines(q, encoding = "UTF-8")
#> [1] "Author: Ángela Zorro Medina"
readBin(q, "raw", 20)
#>  [1] 41 75 74 68 6f 72 3a 20 c3 81 6e 67 65 6c 61 20 5a 6f 72 72

# The path must be one string.
try(wrtxtfb("x", c("a.txt", "b.txt")))
#> Error : wrtxtfb: `path` must be a single non-empty string
